entities.name: José Joaquim Carneiro de Campos
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
José Joaquim Carneiro de Campos, Marquis of Caravelas (1768–1836) was a Brazilian statesman and jurist who was one of the principal drafters of the Brazilian Constitution of 1824 — the first and only constitution of the Brazilian Empire, which remained in effect until the monarchy's fall in 1889. As the leading constitutional drafter, he shaped the document that gave Brazil its distinctive four-power constitutional structure — executive, legislative, judicial, and the 'Moderating Power' held by the emperor that was unique in world constitutional law.

The Moderating Power (Poder Moderador) — derived from Benjamin Constant's constitutional theory — gave Emperor Pedro I the authority to balance and moderate the other three powers, appointing senators, dissolving the Chamber, and appointing ministers.

He had served as Pedro I's Minister of Foreign Affairs and was a founding figure of the Brazilian state after independence (September 7, 1822).

His constitutional work shaped Brazil for 65 years.
